data.why: The repo ships ready-made CSVs matching data/schema.md that exercise both the Campaign-import path (full experiment records including failed/missing-strength rows) and the starter-design path (a space-filling design to print).

goals: set a feedstock composition distribution and print settings on the Bench and see predicted strength, its uncertainty breakdown, and print-success probability for the average batch and for random batches
plan or import a training campaign of print jobs, including a custom CSV of real-looking measurements, and validate it against the schema
train the physics-residual GP strength model and success classifier on the campaign and check calibration on held-out batches

compare robust optimization objectives (nominal, expected, quantile, CVaR, chance-constrained) and see which recommended print settings reduce failure rate or raise expected utility on fresh unseen batches
run the active-learning loop to propose next experiments and track whether true regret falls across rounds
inspect the pre-registered study results from the full Python reproduction to compare the browser's second implementation against the paper's findings

review.summary: The tree follows the README's six-step loop faithfully, and every screen I checked supports its node, so the point, depth and evidence are all sound. It needs small fixes before filing: surface the uncertainty-source breakdown, put the retrain step under the Model task, sharpen three phase labels, and add a study-results feature.
